idea-plugin.name: Staleguard
idea-plugin.description:
Staleguard shows outdated, abandoned, and vulnerable Maven and Gradle dependencies right in the editor: severity-labeled warnings, one-click version bumps, and plain-language advice on which updates matter.

  • Known-vulnerability alerts: versions with published CVEs are flagged with the advisory, its severity, and the first fixed version, checked against the OSV database
  • Inline upgrade hints with major/minor/patch severity and release-age context
  • One-click fixes that correctly edit Maven properties and Gradle version catalogs instead of inlining literals over references
  • Abandonment detection: flags dependencies whose newest release is years old, with the actual date
  • Show What Changed: the release notes between your version and the suggested one, in a dialog, with breaking-change and security banners
  • Team rules: a committed .staleguard.toml shares ignore rules and license policy with the whole team, and Renovate/Dependabot ignores are honored automatically
  • Batch updates with confidence scores, security fixes preselected, plus one-click "apply all patch"
  • Statistics and timeline tool window with license visibility, vulnerability counts, and Markdown/CSV/PNG export
  • Parent POM freshness and a quiet status-bar counter that only appears when something needs attention

Supports pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts, and libs.versions.toml, including androidx and other Google-hosted dependencies and Gradle plugin versions. Works in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio (2024.3 and newer). Stable-only suggestions by default. No telemetry, no accounts: data comes directly from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, the Gradle Plugin Portal, and osv.dev, with a polite 24-hour cache.
